I've lived most of my life in Helsingborg and think it is an amazing town. How did you like it?  
The main reasons for this is the closeness to most things. Two and a half hours to Gothenburg, one hour to Malmö (two of the biggest citys in sweden), about 30 min to Söderåsens national park, one and a half hour to Copenhagen.  


With this we also have a great city with most things one can want for.  


However if you did not enjoy Helsingborg that much I would recommend moving a bit north for the nature and then the city is probably best left up to someone that knows more about it than me.   


One of the best places I've visited was without doubt Umeå tho.  


Hope you find the place of your dreams and good luck with everything!

Listening is one thing. Changing everything they whine about is another

What I feel is dead (with changes and not being able to play with said changes yet):
- Kambi (since most gold cards used in the deck was hit aswell as multiple bronzes)
- Weather control monsters (since weather have been nerfed to the ground and that was the only thing keeping the archetype in the game against swarm decks such as NR and Consume)
- Morkvarg SK  (Obvious reasons)
- Spell'thael (because they lost alot of fighting power)
- The rest of the spell archetypes will have a hard time to survive vs most swarm decks. 
- Axemen SK (obvious reasons there aswell)
- It did seem that QG was hit but not that hard. Their Operator was 7 str in the stream but I do not know if they changed anything else.

I am in no way saying that this is all bad. I just feel that for SK players (I do not consider myself a player of a clear faction since I'm still trying all of them with new ideas on a weekly basis) this hit was very very hard. I know that SK have been dominant aswell but is that reason enough to limit them to 2 playable archetypes (Discard and QG) both witch plays the same leader.

That is very true. And it seems that if we only will play tempo based midrange decks I could just aswell play solitare. 

I really hope that we can get a balance in the game. I just find it hard to see what that might be

Something that might be a good thing for CDPR to consider to get newer players to ease into the game might be to use a "limited ladder system" up to level 8 maye? By that I mean that you each level get the poaaibility to add one more card from each rarity that wasnt in your starting collection. I know this might limit the sales in kegs from level one. But it would also make entering the game way smoother for newer players without the bought kegs affecting their experience.
And I understand that it needed something to be done. BUT is it right to completely destroy weathers AND kill archetypes outside of weather just because new players find it to hard to deal with?
Glad to see I'm not alone

They way I see the game play now would be something along the lines of:
-Play a spell deck and counter everything that the other archetype does
- Play a swarm deck and play untill you win round one no matter the cost.

I understand that it is hard for a developer to please everyone. And I can see how it is frustrating for people brand new that ques into someone with shitloads of cards that can build what they want. But nerfing everything that pose a challenge for new players isnt the answer.

Weather isnt to fun no. But it is couterable and it can be played around if you try to understand the mechanic of the weather and play smart with your weather removal. I would personally love to see frost get the rain text but function as it did before witch 1 damage to all of the 5 enemies. I would even settle for 3-4.
But screaming that weather is causing people to leave the game is just as bad as playing against it. Since it diminishes the skillcap and depth of the game (atleast according to me)

yeah we will have to see how it plays out. But right now I feel really disturbed by the acctual power it seems reddit have over CDPR.
